chunks: As though they had not dwelt there at all. Beware! Condemned were the people of Midian as those of Thamud had been before them!

key_terms.أَلَا: An interjection used for emphasis, warning, or announcement
key_terms.ثَمُودُ: The people of Thamud, an ancient Arab tribe known for Prophet Salih
key_terms.مَدْيَنَ: The people of Midian, descendants of Midan ibn Ibrahim, known for Prophet Shu'ib
key_terms.يَغْنَوْا: To dwell, settle, or reside for a period

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the comparison between the people of Midian and Thamud in Surah Hud?
ai.summary: This verse highlights the total erasure of Midian's legacy following Prophet Shu'ib's call, using the simile 'as if they had never possessed it' to emphasize the completeness of their divine punishment. By linking Midian to Thamud, it reinforces the recurring Quranic theme of distinct yet similar fates for communities that rejected their prophets, serving as a potent warning for the Quraysh and subsequent generations.
